\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شومینه} (shumine)}{شومینه (shumine)}]{\fa{شومینه} (shumine) — a fireplace}

\label{lesson:FA-C535-shumine}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a cushion, then the Persian for a quilt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شومینه}}
\textbf{\fa{شومینه}} (\emph{shumine}) — \textquotedblleft{}a fireplace\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شبهای} \fa{زمستان} \fa{کنار} \fa{شومینه} \fa{مینشینیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shabhâ-ye zemestân kenâr-e shumine mineshinim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
On winter nights we sit by the fireplace.
\end{quote}

An open fireplace; a stove is \emph{bokhâri}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shumine} is a modern loan, usually traced to French \emph{cheminée}, 'fireplace'. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shumine}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shumine}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{shumine}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a cushion, then the Persian for a quilt, then say \emph{shumine} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رختخواب} (rakhtekhâb)}{رختخواب (rakhtekhâb)}]{\fa{رختخواب} (rakhtekhâb) — bedding; a bed (on the floor)}

\label{lesson:FA-C535-rakhtekhab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a quilt, then the Persian for a fireplace.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رختخواب}}
\textbf{\fa{رختخواب}} (\emph{rakhtekhâb}) — \textquotedblleft{}bedding; a bed (on the floor)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادر} \fa{رختخوابها} \fa{را} \fa{پهن} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâdar rakhtekhâbhâ râ pahn kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mother laid out the bedding.
\end{quote}

\emph{rakht} 'clothes, things' + \emph{khâb} 'sleep'. \emph{rakhtekhâb pahn kardan} — to make up a bed on the floor.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rakhtekhâb} is built on two native Persian words, as EtymDB records: \emph{rakht}, 'clothes, gear', and \emph{khâb}, 'sleep' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دنج} (denj)}{دنج (denj)}]{\fa{دنج} (denj) — cosy, quiet (of a place)}

\label{lesson:FA-C535-denj}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a fireplace, then the Persian for bedding.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دنج}}
\textbf{\fa{دنج}} (\emph{denj}) — \textquotedblleft{}cosy, quiet (of a place)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{کافه} \fa{یک} \fa{جای} \fa{دنج} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in kâfe yek jâ-ye denj ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This café is a cosy spot.
\end{quote}

Of a quiet, tucked-away place, not of a person.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{denj} is an everyday Persian word for a quiet, tucked-away place, but EtymDB has no entry for it, and its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خانه} \fa{دار} (khânedâr)}{خانه دار (khânedâr)}]{\fa{خانه} \fa{دار} (khânedâr) — a homemaker}

\label{lesson:FA-C535-khanedar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for bedding, then the Persian for cosy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خانه} \fa{دار}}
\textbf{\fa{خانه} \fa{دار}} (\emph{khânedâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a homemaker\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادرم} \fa{خانه} \fa{دار} \fa{است} \fa{و} \fa{پدرم} \fa{کارمند} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâdaram khânedâr ast va pedaram kârmand ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother is a homemaker and my father is an office worker.
\end{quote}

\emph{khâne} 'house' + \emph{dâr} 'keeping'. \emph{khânedâri} — housekeeping.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khânedâr} is built on native Persian \emph{khâne}, 'house', which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian (EtymDB), and \emph{dâr}, the stem of \emph{dâshtan}, 'to have, to keep'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for bedding, then the Persian for cosy, then say \emph{khânedâr} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کدبانو} (kadbânu)}{کدبانو (kadbânu)}]{\fa{کدبانو} (kadbânu) — a capable housewife; the lady of the house}

\label{lesson:FA-C535-kadbanu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for cosy, then the Persian for a homemaker.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کدبانو}}
\textbf{\fa{کدبانو}} (\emph{kadbânu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a capable housewife; the lady of the house\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادربزرگ} \fa{کدبانو} \fa{است} \fa{و} \fa{همه} \fa{چیز} \fa{را} \fa{خودش} \fa{درست} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâdarbozorg kadbânu ast va hame chiz râ khodash dorost mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandmother is a wonderful homemaker and makes everything herself.
\end{quote}

Warm praise. Built on \emph{kad} 'house' and \emph{bânu} 'lady'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kadbânu} is a native Persian compound, usually explained as \emph{kad}, 'house', and \emph{bânu}, 'lady': the lady of the house. EtymDB has no entry for the compound.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
